Match: match_0001
Innings: 1
Fields:
- inn1.total_runs

Commentary:
Carter was bowled, Gavin was taken, and when Ethan finally went for 49, caught by Adrian Wells off Caleb Stone, the innings had lost the only batter who had made it feel organized. Julian Fox stayed there at the end, Cameron Ross swung hard enough to add a small tail-end lift, and Stoneford eventually reached 144 all out in 35.3 overs, a total that had some defendable quality because the surface was never completely easy, but one that also felt short once the card was read properly. Ethan Drake’s 49 was the clear center, Holt had supplied the early spark, Connor Vale had occupied a little time, and Cameron Ross had added a late flicker, yet the innings depended too heavily on isolated hands.

Innings: 2
Fields:
- inn2.total_runs

Commentary:
Ryan Cross came in and played the right finishing hand, short and clear, while Nolan moved through the last stage unbeaten, ending on 66 from 86 with four boundaries and five sixes. Brookfield reached 145 for 5 in 33.2 overs, and the five-wicket margin fits the day because they had to survive a real top-order wobble before taking command. Stoneford had enough bowling quality to create a contest, especially through Logan Pierce’s 3 for 27, but they did not have enough runs or enough sustained pressure once Nolan and Owen settled.

Match: match_0002
Innings: 1
Fields:
- inn1.total_runs

Commentary:
Owen Clarke added a short bright hand, Connor Wells gave the closing overs a burst with a clean strike over the rope, and even the small late wickets could not erase the central fact that Noah Hart was still there. His unbeaten 101 from 88 balls carried the innings from repair to command, and by the time Harborfield closed on 252 for 8 from 36 overs, the score had a full shape: Rowe and Marsh building the road, Noah becoming the axis, Vale supplying the decisive middle support, and the lower order keeping the last section alive enough to prevent the finish from flattening. Crestview’s bowling had moments rather than control.

Commentary:
Owen Mercer was left not out, but by then the match had long since stopped being a chase. Crestview were all out for 56 in 18.4 overs, with no partnership higher than 13, no batter reaching 15, and almost every phase of the innings broken before it could become a passage. Mason Hart’s 4 for 11 was the spell that shaped the collapse, new ball first, pressure second, and a late return that made the scoreboard look as one-sided as the cricket felt.

Maya Wells was run out before she could settle, Paige went at 66, and the only reason the score moved as far as it did was Hannah Rowe’s late punch.
